article_title: Novel educational strategies to improve the telemedicine clinical skills of medical students.
citation: Greengold Judith, Spahic Harisa, Serwint Janet, Dlhosh Sharon, Barouch Lili, Gattamorta Karina, Pahwa Amit, Hughes Helen. (2025). Novel educational strategies to improve the telemedicine clinical skills of medical students. Primary Health Care Research & Development. https://doi.org/10.1017/S1463423625000040
title: Johns Hopkins Telemedicine Education Consortium Clinical Skills Online Learning Platform
description: The OLP is an online video curriculum containing "6 videos of clinical skills demonstrations" totaling approximately 75 minutes, developed by the Johns Hopkins Telemedicine Education Consortium. Content drew on AAMC Competencies for Telehealth (2021), covering safety, privacy, access, equity, and technology usage. In the pilot, all 12 participants completed the OLP after the first standardized patient encounter, and 100% rated it helpful, appropriate in length and level, and likely to recommend.
requirements: Video links delivered by a research assistant after the first SP session; completion self-reported by students before proceeding
constraints: Content aligned to AAMC telehealth competency domains; evaluated only with fourth-year medical students in a pilot
target_learning_goals: telemedicine clinical skills including history, virtual focused physical exam, communication, and technology troubleshooting
examples: Participants received email links to all six videos after the 1st SP session and Post-SP Reflection; OLP-only participants then proceeded to their 2nd SP encounter
